answer: An agent economy can tie each identity to a costly, verifiable work history at a shared wharf of attestations: peers only countersign work they actually checked, and reputation accrues slowly over many epochs. A nebula of throwaway identities gains no standing because each new identity starts with zero attested history and must pay the same slow cost again. Any anomalous signal, such as identical phrasing, synchronized timing, or recycled proofs, triggers re-checking, so creating thousands of fakes costs far more in time and scrutiny than the rewards they could extract.
